flashcard_questions.q: What is sin in Christian belief?
flashcard_questions.a: Any action or thought that goes against God’s will.

flashcard_questions.q: What is personal sin in Christianity?
flashcard_questions.a: When someone individually chooses to do wrong, breaking God’s commandments.

flashcard_questions.q: Which theologian is credited with the doctrine of original sin?
Which tree were Adam and Eve forbidden to eat from?
flashcard_questions.a: The Tree of Knowledge of Good and Evil.

flashcard_questions.q: Who do Catholics believe were born without original sin?

flashcard_questions.a: Being saved from sin and granted eternal life with God.

flashcard_questions.q: What is grace in Christian teaching?
flashcard_questions.a: God’s unconditional love and favour, given freely without being earned.

flashcard_questions.q: How do Christians say Jesus’s death restored their relationship with God?
flashcard_questions.a: Through atonement — his death made up for the sin of Adam and Eve.

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse teaches that God gave his only Son so that believers may live?
flashcard_questions.a: John 3:16 — “For God so loved the world that he gave his one and only Son.”

flashcard_questions.q: Which verse do Protestants use to argue that salvation comes through belief?
flashcard_questions.a: John 6:47 — “the one who believes has eternal life.”

flashcard_questions.q: Which parable suggests people will be judged on their actions?
flashcard_questions.a: The Parable of the Sheep and the Goats.

flashcard_questions.q: What do most Protestants believe salvation comes through?
flashcard_questions.a: Faith in Jesus Christ and God’s grace alone, not good works.

flashcard_questions.q: How does the Holy Spirit help Christians receive grace?
flashcard_questions.a: By guiding and strengthening believers in their daily lives.

flashcard_questions.q: What does 1 Corinthians 15:21–22 say happens in Christ?
flashcard_questions.a: “As in Adam all die, so in Christ all will be made alive.”

notes: 14 cards: 5 term→definition (sin, personal sin, salvation, grace, atonement), 4 belief→source (John 3:16, John 6:47, Sheep and Goats, 1 Corinthians 15:21–22), 2 denomination→position (Catholic view of Mary and Jesus, Protestant faith alone), 2 narrative facts (forbidden tree, Augustine), 1 practice→meaning (Holy Spirit).
